stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## task-3187787a — panel count encoding (confirmed 2026-10-21)

Divide the input at full separator rows and columns. Each rectangular panel becomes one output cell. In each panel, count cells of the minority/marked color (the color other than the dominant background). Output `1` when that count is exactly 2; otherwise output the panel's background color. Ignore separator lines. Tile sizes and separator/background/marked colors can vary across instances.

Evidence:
- Demo 1 (19x11): separators 7; background 5, marks 9; panels 3x2; output 5x4. Output is 1 exactly for panels containing two 9s, otherwise 5.
- Demo 2 (7x8): separators 9; panel colors mostly 8 with some 7s; panels 3x2; output 2x3 `[[1,1,8],[1,1,1]]`. Each output 1 corresponds to exactly two 7s in that panel; panel with one 7 returns background 8.
- Solved test (24x24): separator 2; background 7, marks 4; panels 4x4; output 5x5:
`[[7,1,7,7,1],[1,1,7,7,7],[1,7,7,7,1],[7,1,7,7,7],[1,7,7,1,7]]`.

Implementation checklist: locate full separator rows/columns, split the remaining strips into panels, determine panel background (dominant color), count non-background cells, and encode exactly-two as 1; otherwise emit background. This supersedes the earlier inaccurate note that described a different task geometry/output.

## task-38f4fc52 — separator-grid uniform-corner rule (confirmed 2026-10-21)

The input is a regular grid of large panels separated by horizontal/vertical lines. The separator intersections (lattice nodes) are usually separator color, with selected nodes changed to marker colors. Extract one output cell for each rectangular panel, i.e. each pair of consecutive horizontal separator lines × pair of consecutive vertical separator lines. For each panel, inspect its four corner lattice nodes: if all four are the same non-background marker color, output that color; otherwise output the dominant interior/panel background color. Ignore the panel interiors and separator thickness. Output dimensions are (# horizontal separator intervals) × (# vertical separator intervals); spacing and palette vary.

Confirmed with demos:
- Demo 1: separator 9, panel background 8; output 2×6. Four same-color 3 corners or 2 corners yield 3 or 2; same-color 5 corners yield 5; all other panels output 8.
- Demo 2: separator 6, background 7; output 4×3. For each panel, all four corners must agree: e.g. output 4, 4, 7 in first row; on the last row, corners encode 8, mixed 8/2, and 2, yielding [8,7,2].
- Demo 3: output 2×1 of 9; both panels have all four corners marked 9.
- Solved test: separator 4, background 8, marker 3; separator intersections at rows 0,14,28 and columns 1,6,11,16,21,26. All-four-3 panels produce `[[8,8,8,8,3],[3,8,8,8,8]]`; mismatched/unmarked corners produce 8.

Checklist: locate regularly spaced separator rows and columns; inspect only the lattice values at their crossings; infer background from panel fill; for each adjacent-node rectangle output the common color iff all four corners are equal to a non-background marker, else background. Do not output the separator lines themselves, marker positions alone, or neighboring-pair summaries.
